title: Anti-Inflammatory Thrombolytic JX10 (TMS-007) in Late Presentation of Acute Ischemic Stroke
summary: In a Japanese phase 2a trial, 90 patients with ischemic stroke ineligible for standard thrombolysis or thrombectomy received JX10 or placebo within 12 hours of last known normal. The primary 24-hour symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage endpoint occurred in 0/52 versus 1/38 patients; the JX10 confidence interval still allowed a 5.6% risk. Day-90 mRS 0–1 favored pooled JX10 doses (40.4% versus 18.4%; adjusted OR 3.34, 95% CI 1.11–10.07), but this was an exploratory secondary outcome without multiplicity adjustment.
findings: Primary hemorrhage endpoint: 0/52 (95% CI 0–5.6%) versus 1/38 (2.6%, 95% CI 0.1–13.8%); P=0.42.
Day-90 mRS 0–2: 28/52 versus 14/38; OR 2.01 (95% CI 0.83–4.86), an uncertain secondary result.
Extracranial bleeding through day 7: 11/52 versus 5/38; no investigator-assessed major bleeding in either group. These small counts do not establish equivalence.
population: Japanese adults with ischemic stroke, NIHSS 6–23, unable to receive tPA or thrombectomy; men aged 20–88 and women aged 60–88; MRI-based screening.
limitations: Small, industry-funded dose-escalation study with pooled doses, no active thrombolytic comparator, restricted Japanese enrollment and exclusion of women younger than 60. Sparse bleeding events cannot establish safety; supplements and a complete full-text appraisal were not reviewed.
intervention: Investigational JX10 1, 3 or 6 mg/kg IV, maximum 360 mg: 10% over 1 minute, then 90% over 30 minutes; 52 patients pooled across sequential dose cohorts.
whyItMatters: A worthwhile signal for future late-window reperfusion research, without evidence to replace established reperfusion selection or introduce JX10 into routine ED treatment.
evidenceNotes: Complete primary abstract and selected indexed PMC methods, results, harms and limitations were reviewed; direct PMC returned a browser challenge and AHA returned 403. No complete full-text or supplement review is claimed. Publisher indexed archive states originally published November 7, 2024, consistent with PubMed/PMC and sponsor's November 8 publication notice. Exact DOI/title correction and retraction searches identified no specific notice; this is not an exhaustive guarantee. Later official ORION registry jRCT2021250014 and sponsor pipeline describe an ongoing phase 2/3 trial, not confirmatory results. Historical paper language about tenecteplase approval and time windows must not be used as current guidance. Next: legal supplement and registry/protocol comparison, complete appraisal, and subsequent ORION results.
primaryEndpoint: Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage with NIHSS worsening of at least 4 points within 24 hours.
